system.name: Canopus
system.description: The second brightest star in the night sky and a historic navigation reference. Canopus is a yellow-white supergiant (F0 Ib) about 313 light-years distant, so luminous it outshines the Sun by 10,700 times.

canopus.name: Canopus
canopus.description: An F0 II bright giant or supergiant about 71 times the Sun's diameter. Canopus is so luminous that NASA uses it as a stable reference point for spacecraft navigation — many deep-space probes carry dedicated star trackers pointed at Canopus to determine their orientation.
canopus.funFact: Canopus is so bright that NASA has used it for over 50 years as a navigation star for deep-space probes — from the Mariner and Voyager missions to the New Horizons spacecraft that visited Pluto.
